governing_synthesis.d1: Official Dukascopy HDE contains 22985 BID tick rows for the fixed interval while JForex getTicks returned 0; exact cross-interface discrepancy proven.
governing_synthesis.d2: Zero-byte cache chunk and disk-cache call path proven; cache-state explanation supported but not causally proven.
governing_synthesis.d3: Fresh-cache causal test never reached history request because connection failed; no cache causality test occurred.
governing_synthesis.f1: D3 connection failure was not an explicit provider rejection; 30-second collector observability was insufficient to isolate connection stage.
governing_synthesis.f2: Same SDK/API/DEMO stack reached full connection within original 30-second bound; transient/state-dependent D3 failure supported, unique cause not proven.

unresolved_questions: Would IHistory.getTicks return nonzero ticks on one fresh-cache, successfully connected attempt for the same fixed interval?
If nonzero, is the JForex canonical payload repeatable byte-for-byte across independent reads?
Can JForex output achieve exact cross-interface parity for timestamps, bid, ask, volumes, order and boundaries?
What exact cause produced the original zero-tick result?
Can any non-S3 path satisfy the Lane-B raw/provider-object identity and integrity claims required to demote AWS criticality?

newly_proven: One fresh-cache JForex history attempt can operationally deliver nonzero ticks for the fixed interval.
Permanent inability of this SDK/API/DEMO stack to deliver any history for the interval would be rejected.
remains_unproven: Existing D1 HDE is insufficient for exact parity because it is BID-only and observed at second precision.
Raw provider-object identity / BI5 object identity.

newly_proven: Zero-tick behavior can recur despite fresh cache and a separately demonstrated viable connection path.
causal_effect: Pure stale-zero-byte-cache explanation would be materially weakened.
A deeper JForex history-delivery/session/provider-specific issue would be strengthened.

newly_proven: The initial READ_A timeout class can recur.
A more specific history-load failure class may become observable if an exact exception is produced.
counterfactuals.limitation: Unless deterministic and path-closing, exact classification narrows mechanism but cannot satisfy raw-object substitution requirements.

voi_tests.name: DECISION_REVERSIBILITY
voi_tests.finding: No H1-H4 outcome changes the decision that JForex cannot by one API history experiment establish the raw-object claims required by the current Lane-B/AWS evidence model.

voi_tests.name: FAIL_INFORMATION_VALUE
voi_tests.finding: H2/H3/H4 mostly reproduce or refine already represented failure classes; they do not alter AWS substitution.

voi_tests.name: SUCCESS_INFORMATION_VALUE
voi_tests.finding: H1 would establish one-attempt operational JForex history delivery, but not repeatability, exact parity, raw-object identity or AWS substitution.

voi_tests.name: PATH_DECISION_IMPACT
voi_tests.finding: AWS-substitute action is invariant. Secondary-interface confidence could change, but there is no current governed need requiring that decision now.

voi_tests.name: UNIQUE_INFORMATION
voi_tests.finding: Fresh-cache history behavior remains scientifically unresolved, but the unresolved fact is not necessary to decide the AWS-substitute path.

voi_tests.name: SUBSTITUTE_RELEVANCE
voi_tests.finding: JForex returns a canonicalized API representation, not the S3 raw object identity required by the current Lane-B model.

voi_tests.name: FUTURE_UTILITY_OUTSIDE_AWS_SUBSTITUTION
voi_tests.finding: JForex retains plausible value as an official Dukascopy content interface, secondary cross-interface check and non-raw validation channel; that future utility does not require another experiment now.

aws_substitution_relevance.jf02_contract_purpose: AWS-independent official Dukascopy provider-history evidence model without claiming S3 raw-object equivalence.

recommendation.reason: The current AWS-substitute decision is invariant across H1-H4, while even H1 would trigger additional repeatability/parity work and still could not establish raw-object identity.
